old_caption:
The video captures a kitchen scene where a glass of water is placed on an induction cooktop. The cooktop is black and has a digital control panel visible on its right side. To the left of the glass, there is a clear glass baking dish. In the background, a tiled backsplash with a blue-gray pattern adds a decorative touch to the setting. Various kitchen items are arranged on the countertop to the right of the cooktop, including a pink mug, a small bowl, a bottle of oil, and some spice containers.

A hand enters the frame from the right side, gesturing towards the cooktop. The hand appears to be pointing at or touching the surface of the cooktop, possibly indicating something about it or preparing to use it. The hand's movement suggests interaction with the cooktop, though no specific action is performed in these frames. The overall scene remains static except for the hand's brief appearance and gesture.

caption: The video captures a kitchen counter against a blue-grey tiled backsplash, its glossy black induction cooktop reflecting the objects placed upon it. A tall clear drinking glass filled with water stands near the center, a faint diagonal refraction line crossing its interior. To the left rests an empty rectangular glass baking dish. To the right, an oil dispenser and spice jars stand near the wall, while a small blue cup, a pink patterned mug, a wooden spoon and chopsticks rest on a wire rack. The water level and every item's position remain unchanged throughout the excerpt. A person's hand is partially visible at the right edge, its fingers occasionally appearing and receding against the wooden trim. The hand never contacts the glass, the dish, or the rack items, and no object is picked up, shifted, or removed. The diagonal line inside the glass holds its place, consistent with a static refraction.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
